RAP payment for AGI $55,000.00 with 1 dependent(s): $179.17 a month (AGI over $50,000 up to $60,000: 5% of the whole AGI; base $229.17 a month minus $50.00 for dependents). On $40,000.00 at 6.53%, month one accrues $217.67 interest; $38.50 is waived and the Department adds a $50.00 principal match, so the balance falls to $39,950.00. At constant income, $21,830.57 would be cancelled after 360 qualifying payments (total paid $64,501.20).

General information, not financial or legal advice. Your servicer computes the official payment from your certified income and loan records. Use the StudentAid.gov Loan Simulator to confirm.

structuredContent.band: AGI over $50,000 up to $60,000: 5% of the whole AGI
notes: AGI is the borrower's (and spouse's, unless married filing separately) adjusted gross income from the most recent tax year.
Dependents are IRC sec. 152 dependents; if married filing separately, only those the borrower claims on that return.

Each on-time payment that does not cover the month's interest: the unpaid interest is not charged. If it lowers principal by less than $50, the Department reduces principal so the total drop equals the lesser of $50 or the payment.
After 360 qualifying monthly payments the remaining balance is cancelled. RAP payments count for PSLF.
Parent PLUS loans and consolidation loans that repaid them (excepted loans) cannot use RAP.
structuredContent.regulation_note: The RAP formula, the $10 minimum, the $50-per-dependent reduction, the interest subsidy, the $50 principal match and the 360-payment cancellation are fixed by statute (HEA sec. 455(q), added by P.L. 119-21 sec. 82001(d)). How a servicer rounds, accrues daily interest, applies the subsidy across several loans and treats a mid-year income change is set by Department of Education procedures and regulations, which this server did not confirm as final on 2026-11-02. Treat cents-level results as estimates.
